title: Candlemas (2 February)
hook: the Presentation: candles blessed for the year, a light to the Gentiles

segments.voice: Yesterday, Ananias: no horse, a light, and a frightened man named Ananias who said brother. Your line was the persecutor turned. Whom did you leave a door open for? Day six hundred forty-nine.

February 2 is Groundhog Day in America: a furry weather forecaster in Pennsylvania, a crowd in the cold, six more weeks of winter or an early spring. The date has an older name. In Europe it was Candlemas, the day people carried candles to church to be blessed, and an old country saying held that a sunny Candlemas meant more winter to come. The usual story is that the groundhog inherited that weather lore. The church kept the candles. Today, forty days after Christmas, a light comes into the temple.
screen: `GROUNDHOG DAY.` → `OLDER WEATHER LORE.` → `FORTY DAYS AFTER CHRISTMAS.`

segments.voice: Luke tells it. Forty days after the birth, Mary and Joseph bring the baby to the temple in Jerusalem to do what the law of Moses asked: a firstborn son presented to the Lord, and an offering for the mother's purification. They bring a pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons, which the law allowed for families who couldn't afford a lamb. A poor family, quietly keeping the rules. Then a man named Simeon, who had been told he wouldn't die before seeing the Lord's anointed, takes the child in his arms and blesses God. The Church still sings his words every night at the end of Night Prayer, in Latin called the Nunc dimittis, now dismiss. He says he can go in peace, for his eyes have seen salvation, and he calls the child, in the Douay-Rheims: "A light to the revelation of the Gentiles, and the glory of thy people Israel." A light for the nations outside Israel, and glory for Israel itself, both at once. Then he turns to Mary and warns her that a sword will pierce her own soul. And an aged widow named Anna, who never leaves the temple, comes up and speaks of the child to all who are waiting. Tradition ties the day's custom to that line about light. On this day the priest blesses candles, and the people walk into church with them lit, carrying the light the way Simeon carried the child. Some families take blessed candles home to light through the year, during storms, sickness and at the bedside of the dying. Since 1997 it has also been the World Day for Consecrated Life, for nuns, religious brothers and others vowed to God, often seen holding candles today.
screen: `FORTY DAYS, TWO TURTLEDOVES.` · `SIMEON TAKES HIM IN HIS ARMS.` · `A SWORD, AND ANNA.` · `CANDLES CARRIED IN, CARRIED HOME.` · then, large: `A LIGHT TO THE REVELATION OF THE GENTILES.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: light a candle, blessed if you have one. If there's a candle in your house from church, light it; if not, any candle. Sit with the flame. Think of Simeon, who had waited a long time and then held what he'd been waiting for. What have you been waiting for a long time? Let it be there with the light, without demanding an answer. If you pray, you can pray Simeon's words, now thou dost dismiss thy servant in peace. If you don't, simply let the flame keep you company. The bell holds the time.
Candlemas. The old name for the Presentation of the Lord on February 2, when candles are blessed and carried, forty days after Christmas. Today's word.
Your line: a light to the nations. Today, be some light for someone who isn't in your usual circle. Day six hundred forty-nine.

howItsDone: On February 2, the feast of the Presentation of the Lord, Catholic parishes bless candles and may begin Mass with a candlelit procession; some people take blessed candles home for use through the year.

original.note: Latin: now you dismiss, the first words of Simeon's song in Luke 2:29.

trapdoor: what you thought: Candlemas is about candles.
what it means: the Presentation of Jesus in the temple, when Simeon called him a light to the nations; the candles carry that light.
what a scholar hears: Luke joins two laws, the firstborn's presentation (Exodus 13) and the mother's purification (Leviticus 12), with the poor family's offering of birds.

notes: Groundhog Day's link to European Candlemas weather lore (via German immigrants in Pennsylvania) is widely cited. Confirm.

Practice paraphrases Luke 2:29 in an older English form ('now thou dost dismiss thy servant ... in peace') without quotation marks; DR reads 'Now thou dost dismiss thy servant, O Lord, according to thy word in peace'.
Use of blessed candles at home (storms, sickness, the dying) is a traditional custom; varies by region.
World Day for Consecrated Life instituted 1997 by John Paul II. Confirm.

Editor review (2026-10-01): Luke does not call Simeon old or say he waited his whole life, fixed; Simeon 'blesses God' (Luke 2:28); groundhog lore and custom origins softened to 'the usual story' and 'tradition'; 'few people know' and 'many' claims cut.
